PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.

items.rationale: Sections 2.4.3(a) and 7.1.7(c) cover like-for-like fittings needed to reconnect the failed heating pipe. Four elbows benchmark at €42 gross, subject to confirmation that this batch was used.
Four elbows benchmark at €42 gross if this distinct model was also needed. Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) exclude a duplicate charge or a second batch not supported by the repair records.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary matching fittings, but §7.1.8(e) requires evidence of a 28 mm connection and five elbows on this short repair. If confirmed, the five-piece benchmark is €104 gross.
The brief repair description does not substantiate five additional 28 mm bends under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.8(e). If all five were needed for the documented reconnection, the benchmark is €103 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) allows a matching elbow used in the reconnection, at about €21 gross for one. Its diameter and use still need to be reconciled with the documented repair under §7.1.8(e).
Section 7.1.7(c) covers fixings used in the repair. Eight screws at the reference rate of about €1.16 each total €9.30 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary supports, but the 10 mm size is not explained by the documented 15 mm replacement pipe. If these clamps supported affected pipework, four benchmark at €19.20 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary clamps matching the repaired 15 mm pipe. Four at about €5.50 each total €22 gross.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary labour for cutting out and reconnecting the failed pipe. The gross benchmark for 6.75 hours is €619.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary helper labour, and the account confirms that a helper attended for part of the job. The gross benchmark for 5.75 hours is €409.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(e) limit payment to the roughly one metre documented as replaced, rather than the 6.4 m billed. At the reference rate of €15.40 per metre, the supported portion is €15.40 gross.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows one travel charge per contractor per invoice for the repair. The first charge benchmarks at €80 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers installation consumables used in the repair, but §7.1.8(c) excludes items already billed separately. The reference allowance for one nonduplicative lot is €43 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes processing fees billed in addition to labour and materials. The positive figure is a conditional placeholder only.

Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like insulation, but §7.1.8(e) limits the quantity to the roughly one metre documented as re-insulated. The six-metre benchmark of €135 gives €22.50 gross for that metre.

Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) rule out duplicate insulation charges and unsupported quantities; no separate mat installation is documented. If a distinct mat was necessary on the short repair, a modest allowance is €20 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers wire used to secure the replacement insulation. The two-piece benchmark is €26 gross if both pieces were needed.

The reported day and a half broadly supports a second block of technician time. Under §§7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(c), €642 gross is reasonable for seven additional repair hours if distinct from the first block and the separately billed cleaning.
Section 7.1.7(f) limits the contractor to the first travel charge on this invoice for the same repair, even if a return visit was needed. The conditional benchmark for one trip is €80 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes contractor protective equipment, including gloves. If separately evidenced repair consumables can be distinguished from the kit, a modest allowance would be €10 gross.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of removed pipe and insulation without double counting. One small disposal charge benchmarks at €60 gross.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(a) distinguish necessary cleanup of leak residues from general hygiene work or an added coating; no coating damage is documented. If the localized cleanup can be separated and substantiated, about €105 gross is reasonable, not the full five-hour package.
